title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction:
Problem: transverse vibrations of a free–free elastic rod of length a, in Euler–Bernoulli theory. The previous page writes the spatial factor as y = α e^{s/f} + β e^{-s/f} + γ sin(s/f) + δ cos(s/f). The conditions y''=y'''=0 at s=0 give δ=α+β and γ=α−β. The same conditions at s=a reduce to the frequency equation cos ω · cosh ω = 1, with ω = a/f.

On this page, for each nonzero root ω, Euler sets f = a/ω, so k = f^4/(bc²) = a^4/(bc²ω^4). The time factor sin(ζ + t√(2g/k)) then has √(2g/k) = cω²√(2bg)/a². The time of one (half-period) 'vibration' is π a²/(ω² c √(2gb)), and the 'sound' (number of vibrations per unit time) is its reciprocal, ω² c √(2gb)/(π a²). So the frequencies scale as ω_n², with ω_n the roots of cos ω cosh ω = 1.

To get the mode shape he uses cos ω = 1/cosh ω, which gives sin ω = ±tanh ω. He substitutes into the first expression for α/β from the previous page and clears the denominator e^ω+e^{-ω}. This gives α/β = (1 − e^{-2ω} − e^ω + e^{-ω})/(−1 + e^{2ω} − e^ω + e^{-ω}). Multiplying by e^ω, the numerator becomes exactly minus the denominator, so α/β = −e^{-ω} when sin ω>0. The other sign gives α/β = +e^{-ω}. Taking α=1 yields β = ∓e^ω, γ = 1 ± e^ω and δ = 1 ∓ e^ω.

With u = s/a, the complete normal-mode solution is y = C sin(ζ + t ω²c√(2gb)/a²) · [e^{uω} ∓ e^{ω(1−u)} + (1±e^ω) sin uω + (1∓e^ω) cos uω]. This is the standard free–free beam mode. The two sign cases (sin ω = ±tanh ω, equivalently tan(ω/2) = ±tanh(ω/2)) separate the modes into the two symmetry classes about the midpoint. Euler does not say this explicitly here. The following page begins locating the roots: the first nonzero one lies a little above 3π/2.
errors: The algebra on this page checks out. sin ω = ±tanh ω follows from cos ω cosh ω = 1. The cleared expression for α/β correctly uses the first of the two equivalent ratios from the previous page. The ratio indeed equals −1 after multiplying by e^ω. β, γ, δ and the mode shape all agree with the standard free–free solution.
The printed text has typos in the substitution sentence. It reads 'ob f = a/φ esse s/f = s/ω' (should be f = a/ω, so s/f = sω/a) and 'ponatur s/a = ω' (should be s/a = u, so s/f = uω).
Minor: what Euler calls 'tempus vnius vibrationis' is a half-period (π/√(2g/k)). This is consistent with his usual convention, not an error.
Next page, Corollary 1 (not this page): writing cos ω (e^ω+e^{-ω}) = 2(1 − ω^4/6) silently truncates the series. The argument that no root lies in the first quadrant is heuristic at that point.

ideas.what: Frequency equation cos ω cosh ω = 1 for the free–free elastic rod, with frequencies proportional to ω_n²/a²
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli (c. 1735–1744; Euler's Methodus inveniendi, Additamentum I, 1744)
ideas.where_published: E65 Additamentum I (1744); E526 revisits it (as discussed in Truesdell 1960, Opera omnia II.11/2)

ideas.what: Explicit normal-mode shape via α/β = ∓e^{-ω}, with γ and δ determined
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (also in later standard texts, e.g. Rayleigh's Theory of Sound)
ideas.where_published: E526 itself; similar forms in Euler's earlier elastic-vibration papers

ideas.what: Splitting by the sign of sin ω = ±tanh ω, equivalent to tan(ω/2) = ±tanh(ω/2)
ideas.modern_name: Factorisation of the frequency equation into even and odd mode families
ideas.where_published: unsure whether Euler states the half-angle factorisation explicitly

deep.surprise_reason: This is a correct, standard derivation of the free–free beam mode shapes and frequencies. The material is well documented in Truesdell's history of elasticity, and nothing on the page appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'ob f=\frac{a}{\phi}' — the print appears to read φ but should be ω: f = a/ω.
'\frac{s}{f}=\frac{s}{\omega}' should be \frac{s}{f}=\frac{s\omega}{a} (printing typo in the original).
'ponatur breuitatis gratia \frac{s}{a}=\omega' should be \frac{s}{a}=u (as required by the following 's/f = uω').
'k=\frac{a^4}{bcc\omega^4}' is correct as transcribed; '\sqrt{2g/k}=c\omega\omega\sqrt{2bg}/aa' is correct.
